item.title: B.C. organization enters debate on government-run grocery amid rising food costs
item.description: VANCOUVER — When Elizabeth Osinde arrived in Canada about two years ago as a refugee from Kenya, pregnant with her son, she remembers being able to buy a bunch of kale for $2 or $3. That same bunch is now closer to $5.

item.title: Grand jury refuses to indict Democratic lawmakers in connection with illegal military orders video
item.description: WASHINGTON (AP) — A grand jury in Washington refused Tuesday to indict Democratic lawmakers in connection with a video in which they urged U.S. military members to resist “illegal orders,” according to a person familiar with the matter.

item.title: Ottawa 'probably' will announce winner of submarine contract this year: MP
item.description: OTTAWA — The federal government may name the winner of the heated competition to supply the navy with a fleet of new submarines as soon as this year.

item.title: Carney suspends trip to Europe following B.C. school shooting
item.description: OTTAWA — Prime Minister Mark Carney suspended his plans to travel to Halifax and Munich, Germany, following a deadly school shooting in British Columbia. Carney said in a statement he is devastated by the horrific shooting in Tumbler Ridge, B.C.

item.title: 10 dead, including female suspect, in 'devastating' shootings at B.C. school and home
item.description: TUMBLER RIDGE, BRITISH COLUMBIA — RCMP say eight people, including the female suspect, are dead after a shooting at a school in Tumbler Ridge, B.C., while two more bodies were found at a home believed to be connected to the incident.

item.title: Voices in reaction to the mass shooting that left 10 dead in Tumbler Ridge, B.C.
item.description: RCMP say seven people were killed when a shooter entered a high school in Tumbler Ridge, B.C., on Tuesday, and then they killed themself. More than two dozen others were hurt, some of them seriously.
